cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Count What I Did
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to count the trips, not just the shopping. Twelve bags up six flights before you call that a quick errand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Sit down; I'll put them away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've remembered one recovery step. The frozen peas needed a second trip, so I'm not done being tired.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then have two rests. I'll make tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally counting properly. Tell the others why I get two; I don't want my lesson in recovery mistaken for a whole afternoon off.

reason: Make A grade B increasingly helpful response as proper labor accounting and use the two-rest offer to request visible credit rather than only comfort.
